newsitem.title: USA: Ford Louisville plant halted by floods.
newsitem.headline: Ford Louisville plant halted by floods.

text.p: Ford Motor Co was forced to suspend production for one shift at its Louisville Assembly plant Monday morning after heavy rains prohibited employees from getting to work and flooded a holding area with 800 to 1,000 light trucks.

Ford spokesman Bill Carroll said water had subsided enough for the afternoon shift to resume production at the plant. About 1,700 Explorer sport/utilities and Ranger compact pickup trucks are made during each 10-hour shift.
Ford sent teams of insurance inspectors and others to the plant to determine if anything from the Explorers and Rangers caught in the holding area can be salvaged.
"About all we can do now is check them all over, see what we can save and what we can't save," said Carroll.

The Louisville area received about 11 inches of rain over the weekend. The downpour caused flooding that submerged some of the vehicles past their hoods. The vehicles had just been completed and were being held in the convoy area for shipment to dealers this morning, said Carroll.

Except for a small amount of water in the cafeteria, the Louisville plant itself was not damaged, Carroll said. In addition to Lousville, Ford makes the popular Explorer at its St. Louis Assembly plant.
Ford has the ability to recoup lost production at the Louisville plant by scheduling more overtime, Carroll said.

Ford's Kentucky Truck Assembly facility, which makes commercial light, medium and heavy duty trucks, is located on higher ground in another part of the city and was not affected by the flooding, said Carroll.
